               <ns0:p n="28">28 For which of you intending to build a towre, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost, whether ye have <ns0:hi>sufficient</ns0:hi> to finish <ns0:hi>it</ns0:hi>?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="29">29 Lest haply after he hath laid the foundation, and is not able to finish <ns0:hi>it,</ns0:hi> all that behold <ns0:hi>it,</ns0:hi> begin to mock him.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="30">30 Saying, This man began to build, and was not able to finish.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="31">31 Or what king going to make war against a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nother king, sitteth not down first, and consulteth whether he be able with ten thousand to meet him that cometh against him with twenty thousand?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="32">32 Or else, while the other is yet a great way off, he sendeth an ambassage, and desireth conditions of peace.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="33">33 So likewise, whosoever he be of you, that forsaketh not all that he hath, he cannot be my dis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ciple.<ns0:note place="bottom">Our Lord, had in the Parable of the Supper shewed what those things are, which keep Men from imbracing the Call of the Go<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />spel; to wit their Hearts too much adherence to, and imbracing of Sensible, and Sensual things. For the according of which Temp<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tation he had told them, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 25, 26, 27. That if they loved any thing in the World more than him, they could have no Portion <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> him, they could not be his Disciples, for (as <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> saith) they are not worthy of him. Nay, more than this, they must <ns0:hi>take up,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>bear their Cross,</ns0:hi> and come after him. Here he directs them the best Expedient in order to the performance of these Du<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ties, so hard to Flesh and Blood. That is, to sit down before Hand, and think what it will cost them to go through with the Profession of Religion. This he tells them, ordinary <ns0:hi>Prudence</ns0:hi> directeth men to, when they go about to Build, or Fight. As to the first they make as good an Estimate as they can of the Charge. As to the latter they consider both the charge, and the Strength that they are able to produce, to make opposition. So saith he, must they do who will be his Disciples, 1. Sit down and consider what it will cost them to bec<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>me the Lords <ns0:hi>Building,</ns0:hi> what old Foundation of Nature must be digged up, what new Foundati<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on must be laid, how many Stones must be laid before they can come up to a Wall <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>evel, to the promise wherein Salvation is in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sured. 2. Then they must consider what <ns0:hi>Oppositions</ns0:hi> they are like to meet with, from the World, the Flesh and the Devil. And they must be ready to forsake all for Christ, tho it may be they shall not be Actually called out to it. Only we must remember, that in <ns0:hi>Parables</ns0:hi> every Branch is not to be applyed. We must de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sire no Conditions of Peace from our Spiritual Adversaries. 2. In our counting up of our Strength to maintain the Spiritual Fight we must do as Princes use to do, who use to count the Forces of their Allies, and Confederates, as well as their own: So we must not count what opposition we alone can maintain against the World, the Flesh and the Devil; but what Christ (who is in Co<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />venant with us as to these Fights) and we can do together. So as Consideration, and Pre-deliberation here is not required of us up<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on any account to deter us from the Fight (for fight we must, or dye Eternally) but to prepare us for the Fight, by a firm and Steady Resolution, and to help us how to manage the Fight, looking up to Christ for his Strength and Assistance in the Managery of it.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="34">34 Salt <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> good: but if the salt have lost its savour, wherewith shall it be seasoned?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="35">35 It is neither fit for the land, nor yet for the dunghil; <ns0:hi>but</ns0:hi> men cast it out. He that hath ears to hear, let him hear.<ns0:note place="bottom">See the <ns0:hi>Notes</ns0:hi> on <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 5.13. <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> 9.50. where we met with the most of what we have in these Verses. By Salt in this place our Saviour seemeth to mean a Christian Life, and Profes<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sion. It is a good, a noble, a great thing to be a Christian: But one that is so in an outward Profession may lose his Saviour. Tho a Man cannot fall away from Truth, and Reallity of Grace, yet he may fall away from his Profession, he may be given up to believe Lies, and imbrace damnable Errors, he may shake off that dread of God which he seemed to have upon him, and then what is be good for? wherewith shall he be seasoned? He is nei<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther fit for the <ns0:hi>Land</ns0:hi> nor the <ns0:hi>Dunghil,</ns0:hi> as some things will spoil Dunghils, so Debauched Professors do but make wicked Men worse, by prejudicing and hardening them against the ways, and Truths of God. <ns0:hi>He that hath Ears to hear, let him hear.</ns0:hi> It is an usual <ns0:hi>Epiphonema,</ns0:hi> or Sentence by which Christ often shuts up grave, and weighty Discourses; the Sense is, you had therefore need to look about you, and to undertake the Profes<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sion of my Religion upon such weighty Grounds, and Princi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ples as will carry you through the practice of it to the end, a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gainst all the Oppositions you shall meet with; for if you Apo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />statize from your Profession, you will be the worst of Men, nei<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther fit for <ns0:hi>the Church,</ns0:hi> nor for <ns0:hi>the World</ns0:hi> (for you will make that the worse) indeed fit for nothing but for the Fire of Hell.</ns0:note>
